Subdued overcast early morning in a narrow market street of a decaying
18th-century Central European city. Elevated high-angle view, the camera
floating in open air about five metres above the cobbles and tilted down
along the street, which runs diagonally from the lower-right corner into
the upper-left depth, never straight down the middle. Completely clean
unobstructed view: clear open air between the camera and the street, the
whole frame filled edge to edge with the street itself — no window frame,
no window, no balcony, no railing, no arch, no foreground silhouette.

The street is packed wall to wall with a working crowd — bodies shoulder
to shoulder, layered from the foreground into the far haze, only patches
of wet cobblestone showing between the legs. Wooden stalls under dark
sagging canvas awnings line both sides: silver fish on crushed ice, root
vegetables, bread, clay pots, plucked fowl on hooks. Market women in
dirty linen caps sell, customers haggle, porters carry sacks and barrels,
chickens and pigs between the legs, dogs, barefoot children. Three-storey
townhouses with flaking plaster, soot streaks, wrought-iron guild signs,
laundry lines, chimney smoke rising into a flat pale sky. A shallow open
gutter with a faint red-pink trace runs down the street.

Three small scenes live inside this crowd, staggered one behind the other
along the depth of the street, each clear but none dominating:

NEAREST TO THE CAMERA, in the foreground at the lower part of the frame, a
funeral passes through the crowd: a tired horse draws a plain flat wooden
cart carrying a simple unpainted pine coffin, and behind it walk a priest
in a black cassock with a worn book and three weeping women in dark shawls
and white linen caps, heads down; a man at the roadside takes his cap off
as they pass, while most of the crowd simply works on around them.

DEEPER IN THE FRAME, in the middle distance on the shaded right side, a
man and a woman of about thirty stand close together kissing in a deep
dark stone gateway, unaware of the street — he in a worn brown coat and
battered tricorne, she in a grey-green skirt and white cap; a small
barefoot boy in ragged clothes darts through the crowd near their gateway.

AND IN A DOORWAY on the right side of the street, a young mother — barely
twenty and worn down by hard living: her simple light linen summer dress,
faded to a pale dusty blue-grey, is smudged with dirt and ash, the hem
caked with dried street mud, a small tear at the shoulder seam; her head
is uncovered, her hair half fallen out of its pins, loose greasy strands
hanging around a tired young face, a smudge of grime on her cheek and on
her hands — sits alone on a stone step nursing her baby: the infant is
wrapped in a plain stained linen rag, held close to her chest, her body
curved around it so the act itself stays hidden by the child's swaddled
body and the curve of her arm; her head is bowed over the child, quiet and
matter-of-fact — a small still island of calm inside the moving crowd.

Light: fully diffuse overcast skylight, soft and shadowless, no direct
sun, no sunrise warmth. The hazy far end of the street glows pale milky
grey-green and is the brightest part of the image; the distant crowd reads
as dark silhouettes against it; the near foreground sits a stop darker.

Palette: 60% cold grey-green stone and mud, 30% weathered brown wood and
dirty linen, 10% one amber lantern flame, the raw pale pine of the coffin
and faint red in the gutter. Heavily desaturated olive grading, milky
highlights, shadows keeping detail. Everything belongs to the 1780s. Damp
organic textures throughout.
